subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@alphaprod.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned:

What we heard: 
- AlphaProd will be using the assistant for customer support triage + short completions embedded in product flows.
- Expected traffic profile: steady stream of short requests (webhooks from client apps), i.e. continuous low-latency workload rather than large batch jobs.

Your initial numbers / asks (please confirm):
- Estimated monthly token volume: ~250,000,000 total tokens (combined input+output).
- Average per-request token footprint: ~160 tokens (100 input / 60 output) — yields ~1.56M requests/month.
- Target unit economics: ~$30 per 1M tokens (to land within your $6k–$10k/month budget).
- Latency SLO: P95 ~300–500ms for typical requests.

Batching & concurrency notes we flagged on the call:
- Continuous batching expectation: steady arrival rate, so we’ll optimize for small-to-medium batch sizes (target steady-state batch size 8–12) to preserve latency while improving cost.
- Concurrency: you’ll likely need 4–8 concurrent inference workers in peak regions; we’ll baseline on 4 and scale if requests spike.
- Caching / prefix reuse: likely helpful on repeated prompts; we’ll include recommendations in the estimate.

Next steps (action items):
1) I’ll send a pricing estimate and MAP that aligns to the 250M token scenario and shows unit economics at $30 / 1M tokens. (attached: redwood_pricing_estimate_v3.xlsx, MAP).
2) Can you confirm the token estimate and the budget band above? If your expected token volume or target $/1M differs, let me know — we can show alternate scenarios.
3) Security: you asked for SOC 2 + data residency detail — sending SOC 2 summary (attached) and a short note on VPC options.
4) Schedule a follow-up demo for end-to-end integration and a short technical runbook review.

Proposed times next week: Tue 4/27 10–11am PT or Wed 4/28 2–3pm PT. Which works?

Thanks — Camila
--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@alphaprod.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching

Thanks Camila — helpful summary. Confirming the high-level numbers:
- Monthly tokens: we currently estimate 250M combined tokens is reasonable for the first 3 months of roll-out. Could grow 2–3x over the year.
- Target unit economics: $25–$35 per 1M tokens, $30 is the right baseline for evaluation.
- Budget: target monthly spend $6k–$10k initially; open to committed/dedicated pricing if the growth path makes sense.

A couple clarifying questions:
1) For the continuous small-request pattern, what P95 latency do you expect with a continuous batching config (batch size ~8–12) on a single dedicated GPU?
2) Any recommendations on warm-up / pre-warming to reduce cold-starts for steady but spiky traffic?
3) Can you include a 3-scenario table in the estimate (conservative / baseline / scale) with token buckets and corresponding cost?

Also: we need SOC 2 summary + a short blurb on data residency for our procurement. If you can include trial credits and an initial dedicated capacity price (monthly commit) as an option, that would be great.

Will take Tue 4/27 10am PT for the demo.
— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, AlphaProd
alex.johnson@alphaprod.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@alphaprod.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching

Alex — great, thanks for confirming and for the questions. Quick answers and what I’ll include in the follow-up package:

1) Latency with continuous batching:
- For short requests and target batch sizes ~8–12 on modern A100/H100-class capacity, P95 latency in our hosted environment is typically ~200–400ms depending on model (lower for smaller models).
- We’ll include model-specific numbers in the estimate and show tradeoffs (e.g., cheaper quantized variants vs full-precision).

2) Warm-up / pre-warm guidance:
- Keep a minimal steady baseline concurrency (1–2 warm workers) so KV caches stay hot; for traffic spikes configure autoscaling thresholds to add workers quickly.
- We’ll propose a pre-warm policy tuned to your observed qps and target latency.

3) Pricing scenarios: yes — conservative / baseline / scale with token buckets, unit $/1M lines, and a dedicated vs hosted comparison.

Attachments I’ve added here: redwood_pricing_estimate_v3.xlsx (3-scenario table), mutual-action-plan-Acme.pdf, soc2-report-summary.pdf.

I’ll also add a short MAP with milestones, owners, and target dates (PO, security review, signed contract, pilot).

See you Tue 4/27 10am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Camila

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@alphaprod.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching

Thanks Camila — received the attachments and the scenarios look helpful. Couple follow-ups after a quick review:

- Security: SOC 2 summary looks good; procurement will ask for full report later but this will unblock early review. Please add a one-line on data residency / VPC options we can paste into our security questionnaire.
- Trial: can Redwood extend some credits so we can sanity-check latency and batching behavior on our real traffic shape?
- Dedicated capacity: interested in a 3-month committed option; can you include monthly commit pricing and what burst capacity looks like?

Looking forward to the demo on Tue. If you can bring an engineer to demo the pre-warm/autoscale settings that would be ideal.
— Alex

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@alphaprod.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching

Alex — perfect. Confirming the next items: 

- I’ve scheduled the demo for Tue 4/27 10am PT (calendar invite sent). Our solutions engineer, Aditya, will join to walk pre-warm, autoscale, and continuous-batching tuning.
- We’ll include a one-line for data residency / VPC in the MAP and the procurement packet.
- Trial credits: we can provide a short proof-of-concept credit bucket (I’ll include the amount in the formal quote).
- Dedicated capacity: I’ll include 3-month commit pricing, burst pricing, and example throughput for continuous batching (target batch sizes and expected P95 numbers per model).

Expect a formal quote and MAP by end of day 4/30. If anything changes on your side (token estimate or target $/1M), let me know so we can adjust the scenarios.

Thanks — Camila
